reviewed_finding: The sources are general: Paper.lean and Paper001.lean prove, over List A and List alpha with hand-rolled structures, that an isomorphism induces an alphabet bijection (Classical.choice is used for it, per Paper.lean header) and hence equal sizes. Paper001.lean DiscreteEquiv is, by definition, a pair of mutually inverse maps on objects, so no_discrete_equivalence is the pigeonhole fact; the Python checks free_monoids_nonisomorphic and discrete_categories_inequivalent compare counts (the latter returns left != right). The DAG-local Lean theorem pg_to_sn_and_wdp_route_chain_composition is fixed arithmetic and vacuous for this node. This node re-proves the statement with Mathlib FreeMonoid / MulEquiv and Discrete categories (genuine categorical equivalence), bridges the source WordIso to MulEquiv, adds the converse iff, and records the sharp boundary: a set bijection exists, so the obstruction is multiplicativity; native: exact word counts, brute-force atoms, exhaustive homomorphism search with bounded image length, discrete equivalences, shortlex bijection.

claim_boundary.supports: For arbitrary alphabets (kernel-checked, lean4/FreeMonoidNoniso.lean, Mathlib FreeMonoid and CategoryTheory.Discrete): a monoid isomorphism FreeMonoid a ~ FreeMonoid b induces a bijection of the alphabets (the atoms are the one-letter words and an isomorphism permutes atoms), so unequal finite alphabets give non-isomorphic free monoids, and FreeMonoid a ~ FreeMonoid b iff a ~ b; alphabetEquiv, no_free_monoid_iso, freeMonoid_iso_iff_equiv, set_bijection_exists and the discrete-category theorems use Classical.choice (kernel axiom reports: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound), as does the source for the same step; an equivalence of discrete categories Discrete a ~ Discrete b (a genuine CategoryTheory.Equivalence) gives a bijection a ~ b, so Fin n and Fin m give equivalent discrete categories iff n = m; every source WordIso yields a MulEquiv (WordIso.toMulEquiv) and the source theorem is recovered through it; the converse MulEquiv -> WordIso is not stated; the boundary is sharp: for n, m >= 1 the underlying SETS of FreeMonoid (Fin n) and FreeMonoid (Fin m) are in bijection (both countably infinite), so the content is multiplicativity, not cardinality; the free monoid on the empty alphabet is one point; words of length k over Fin n number n^k and atoms number n. Exhaustive native checks on 15 alphabet pairs (sizes 0 to 4): all homomorphisms whose generator images have length <= 1 for the pairs (3,4), (4,3), (4,4) and length <= 2 for all other pairs; the candidates injective on words of length <= 2 whose images contain every letter (a necessary-condition filter, not a proof of bijectivity) are exactly the n! letter permutations when n = m and none otherwise; the equivalences of discrete categories are exactly the bijections; and the explicit shortlex bijection of the underlying sets is multiplicative on the first 30 words exactly when n = m (a prefix statement).
claim_boundary.does_not_support: Any structure on numerals or alphabets other than the free-monoid multiplication or the discrete category (a numeral or alphabet re-presentation may still be a non-isomorphic map, a set bijection, or an isomorphism of some other structure; no other structure, such as free commutative monoids, is examined); language restriction, partial recovery and total erasure (separate ledger row WDP-P001-009); infinite alphabets beyond the general Lean statement; the native homomorphism search covers short generator images only and is an instance, not the general theorem.
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: A monoid isomorphism between free monoids on any two alphabets induces a bijection of the alphabets, so free monoids on finite alphabets of different sizes are not isomorphic and discrete categories with different finite object counts are not equivalent; a bare bijection of the underlying sets does exist for sizes at least one, so a numeral or alphabet re-presentation cannot be an isomorphism of the free-monoid (word concatenation) structure or of the discrete-category structure; other structures are not addressed.
claim_boundary.next_test: Decide which numeral or alphabet re-presentations ARE structure-preserving: classify the monoid homomorphisms between free monoids on different alphabet sizes that are injective (codes) or onto (decoders), and prove which of them preserve atoms, as the next step beyond the isomorphism obstruction proved here.

additional_scope_clarifications.reviewed_target_qualification: Non-isomorphism is established for the free-monoid multiplication (monoid isomorphism) and for discrete-category equivalence; a bare set bijection between unequal infinite alphabets-of-words exists, so the node does not rule out re-presentations that ignore the multiplication.
additional_scope_clarifications.historical_target_status: Original target retained verbatim as source history; the corrected narrow scope governs this run.

second_review.notes: Cold read of run 20261021T132245Z_staged. lean4/FreeMonoidNoniso.lean is byte-identical (sha 97453073...) to the p1 copy; the p2 lean log has the 14 literal axiom reports (isAtom_iff propext+Quot.sound, isAtom_map_iff Quot.sound, free_monoid_zero_subsingleton Quot.sound; everything built on alphabetEquiv/atomEquiv uses Classical.choice). Statement fidelity is good: alphabetEquiv is a def over arbitrary Type* alphabets built from isAtom_iff (atoms = one-letter words; IsAtom is a local definition, not Mathlib's) and isAtom_map_iff; no_free_monoid_iso is for Mathlib MulEquiv of FreeMonoid; freeMonoid_iso_iff_equiv is a true iff; discrete_equivalence_card works on a genuine CategoryTheory.Equivalence via unitIso/counitIso; set_bijection_exists uses countability and needs both alphabets nonempty; WordIso.toMulEquiv is one direction only and supports says so. Earlier-pass amendments are all applied in the final text: WordIso 'yields a MulEquiv, converse not stated'; Classical.choice named with the kernel axiom triple; 'length <= 1 only for the pairs (3,4),(4,3),(4,4), length <= 2 elsewhere' is now correct (matches public_input.json); 'bijective candidates' is described as 'injective on words of length <= 2 whose images contain every letter (a necessary-condition filter, not a proof of bijectivity)'; narrowest_claim is restricted to the free-monoid (concatenation) and discrete-category structures with 'other structures are not addressed'. The rebuild introduced no weakening: the checker still recomputes atoms by complement of 2-products, homs (sum m^k)^n, letters_onto by inclusion-exclusion, injectivity and candidates with string-valued homomorphisms, discrete equivalences as bijective maps, and shortlex via dictionary; keys and ints type-checked; case set compared sorted; 8 semantic mutants all rejected by the expected leaf, order control accepted; checker pin hashes in p2 match the files. Findings the earlier pass missed or underweighted: (1) the certificate field set_bijection is trivially 1 for every n,m>=1 (it tests only that the first 30 shortlex words of one alphabet map injectively onto the first 30 of the other, true for any enumeration) and homomorphism_violations = 0 for n = m is trivial because the shortlex map for n = m is the identity; so the native record gives no evidence for 'a set bijection exists' (that is the Lean theorem set_bijection_exists) and the n = m half of 'multiplicative exactly when n = m' is vacuous. Supports presents it as a prefix statement about one explicit map, so this is not an overclaim, but 'exactly when n = m' reads stronger than it is. (2) narrowest_claim's connective 'a bare bijection ... does exist ..., so a numeral or alphabet re-presentation cannot be an isomorphism' is a non sequitur: the conclusion follows from non-isomorphism, while the bare bijection only shows the obstruction is multiplicativity, not cardinality. (3) 'numeral or alphabet re-presentation' is not formalised; the only formal objects are MulEquiv and Equivalence, so that clause is an interpretation of the DAG wording, bounded by 'other structures are not addressed'. (4) the native homomorphism search is bounded and adds nothing beyond the Lean theorem; supports and does_not_support say so. No false statement inside the claim boundary, no wrong certificate can pass, Lean anchors state what the claim says. next_test (classify injective/onto homomorphisms between free monoids of different sizes and atom preservation) is this node's own unpaid obligation, distinct from does_not_support.

dag_suggestion.statement: Free monoids on alphabets of different finite sizes are not isomorphic (a monoid isomorphism induces a bijection of alphabets via atoms; in general FreeMonoid a is isomorphic to FreeMonoid b iff a and b are in bijection), and discrete categories with different finite object counts are not equivalent. The underlying sets of nonempty free monoids are in bijection, so a numeral/alphabet re-presentation can be a set bijection but cannot be an isomorphism of the free-monoid multiplication or an equivalence of discrete categories; other structures are not addressed.

earlier_pass.notes: lean4/FreeMonoidNoniso.lean (sha identical to p1 copy) recompiles exit 0, 14 axiom reports. Statement fidelity: alphabetEquiv is a general def over arbitrary Type* alphabets; no_free_monoid_iso, freeMonoid_iso_iff_equiv, discrete_equivalence_card / discrete_equivalence_iff (real CategoryTheory.Equivalence, not a restated pigeonhole), set_bijection_exists and bijection_but_not_isomorphic are genuine. Defects of wording: (1) supports says 'the source structure WordIso is the same as a MulEquiv'; Lean proves only WordIso.toMulEquiv (one direction, plus the source theorem recovered through it). The converse MulEquiv -> WordIso is not stated, so 'is the same as' is stronger than the anchor; WordIso is also a re-typed copy (I compared it field by field with Paper.lean line 200: identical), not an import. (2) supports says 'the atoms are the one-letter words and an isomorphism permutes atoms': true (isAtom_iff, isAtom_map_iff). (3) Axioms: alphabetEquiv and everything built on it use Classical.choice (via noncomputable Equiv.ofBijective / subtypeEquiv inverse); the profile never mentions that the isomorphism-to-bijection direction is classical, while the source paper header flags Classical.choice for the same step. Add it to supports. (4) The native evidence is bounded and not independent of the claim: 'bijective candidates' means injective on words of length <= 2 AND every letter occurs among the images of probe words; this is a necessary-condition filter, not 'bijective', and 'letters_onto' counts tuples whose images cover all single-letter words, not surjections of monoids. The record check then re-asserts 'candidates == permutation homs' for d <= 2. Because only generator images of length <= 2 (d<=1 for the pairs (3,4),(4,3),(4,4)) are searched, the profile sentence 'or <= 1 for sizes 3-4' is inaccurate: (3,2,2),(3,3,2),(2,4,2),(4,2,2) use d=2 too. The native check is therefore an instance beyond which the Lean theorem does all the work; the profile does say so in does_not_support. (5) Checker independence is good where claimed: atoms by complement of products (producer uses a split test), inclusion-exclusion for onto-letters, string-valued homs, dictionary-built shortlex; all fields are exact ints, set of cases compared sorted. Not a defect but note: homomorphism_violations is tested against only the first 30 shortlex words, so 'multiplicative on the first 30 words exactly when n=m' is a prefix statement; the n=m=0 and n=0,m>=1 records have set_bijection flags that the checker does not constrain. Mutants: eight near misses, all leaf edits but each rebuts a named misreading (set bijection read as iso, cardinality as the invariant, collapsing surjection as bijection, longer atoms, unequal discrete equivalence, trivial vs one-generator monoid, unique iso, word counts). Missing near miss for the actual unpaid bridge ('re-presentation may be an iso of OTHER structure'): a base-n numeral to base-m numeral bijection that IS additive/ordered-preserving on a quotient, or free monoid vs free commutative monoid / free semigroup (e.g. N^n vs N^m are also non-isomorphic but N vs N^2 sets are bijective), i.e. a record showing the claim is specific to free-monoid multiplication. next_test (classify injective homs / decoders between free monoids of different sizes and which preserve atoms) is this node's own unpaid obligation, not boilerplate, and distinct from does_not_support. DAG: the node text concludes 'a numeral/alphabet re-presentation cannot be an isomorphism of structure', which over-reads: the result covers only the concatenation structure and the discrete-category structure; and the DAG bottleneck 'finite-cardinality argument' is wrong (the argument is atoms, not cardinality; the underlying sets are bijective).
